category_title: Five-year-old students exhibiting school-related frustration and challenging peer interactions
minimal_context: Patrick is sitting at a table with his peers using crayons and paper to create rubbings of tree bark.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is the tree bark, paper, and crayons. Everyone take a spot at the table and start making your bark rubbings.

STUDENT: Hurry up and move, you're in my way!

TUTOR: Let's just try to share the space and use the crayons.

STUDENT: (Kicks the table leg) I don't want to do this with them. They are too slow.

TUTOR: Just put your paper over the bark and rub the crayon on it to see what happens.

STUDENT: I'm bored, bored, bored! I don't want to do rubbings with these crayons!

options.A: Use a digital portfolio app to take notes, organize his work, and archive past bark rubbing projects.
options.B: Place an exclusive display board in the classroom only for Patrick to display his bark rubbings.
options.C: Implement relatively tight timelines for the student to complete the bark rubbings during the group activity.
options.D: Scaffold and support the student's learning by asking questions and offering many different ways to explore the bark.
